interest: Shows US scrutiny of Japanese fishing requests as possible cover for naval reconnaissance in the Gulf of Fonseca.
overview: Two-page docket (Form DS-46, Oct 1945) on Japanese activity in El Salvador, 1933-36: coastal surveys, fishing-concession requests, visitors Yamada and Bampa, a rumored Gulf of Fonseca naval base, talks with President Martinez, and propaganda reports.

people.name: William J. McCafferty
people.role: U.S. Chargé d'Affaires ad interim in El Salvador

subfiles.about: A Department of State docket sheet summarizing documents and cross-references regarding Japanese military, naval, espionage, and commercial activities in El Salvador between 1933 and 1936.
subfiles.summary: Docket (Form DS-46, 1945) indexing 1933-36 reports on Japanese coastal surveys, fishing-concession bids, visitors Yamada and Bampa, a rumored naval base in the Gulf of Fonseca, talks with President Hernández Martínez, and propaganda monitoring.
